chapter_note: This chapter is largely an editorial moral/application unit (unity among hearers) built on a short cosmological premise: the Light’s inherent concord versus the Darkness’ self-division. The core substrate is preserved mainly as statements about internal harmony/order in the Light-realm and internal disunity in the Darkness-realm; the shift to analogy with "the kingdom of this world" and direct second-person exhortation marks later application.

paragraphs.core_text: [Now as to what affects the] Light, behold, at the beginning the Darkness was strong against it; [ ... ] no disunity [ ... ] exists in the Light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution: "Once again the enlightener speaks to his disciples:" (hagiographic compilation frame).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins with a formulaic frame attribution; underneath it is a concise cosmological claim that stays within the Light/Darkness system (harmony in Light), consistent with older impersonal teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] how far [ ... the lig]ht that came forth from [ ... ] in that place in a [ ... ] alone [ ... ] the greatness of the Light with one another for ever, and nor did one of them transgress the command and order that his brother had entrusted to him forever.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Impersonal exposition about the internal order of the Light-realm (no second-person address; no institutional referents). Harmony/obedience is described as a property of the cosmic community itself, not as an exhortation.

paragraphs.core_text: However, the Darkness, the enemy, was doomed and overcome; because of the arising of disharmony it was divided within itself. Even the kingdom was divided within itself; [and] ev[en] the [powers, who had] left their abyss behind and come up fo[llow-ing] it, were doomed because of the disunity that was present in all of them. The Darkness was destroyed, and its other powers were humiliated,
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the closing application/analogy that exits the cosmic system into a contemporary comparison: "because the p[ower] of that first light functions in the same way as the kingdom of this world."
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core mechanism preserved: Darkness’ defeat is explained by internal disharmony (cosmos→cosmos). Final clause pivots to an illustrative comparison with worldly kingdoms (cosmos→this world), signaling later applicative editing.

Illustrative material framed in terms of a "kingdom" gaining glory when its "associates" agree; the language functions as a didactic analogy rather than cosmological system-description, and it no longer anchors explicitly in the Light/Darkness mechanics.
Continues the applicative analogy of one kingdom condemning another; lacks systematic cosmic correspondences and reads as moral-political exemplum supporting the later exhortation.
Direct second-person exhortation (“you yourselves…”) using the teaching to command communal unanimity; this is application voice, not impersonal cosmological exposition.
Continues exhortation with warning and optative aside (“may it not happen!”). Even where Sin is personified, the paragraph is wholly a behavioral application to the community.
Imperatival paraenesis (“Neither be divided… and you will conquer…”), focused on community conduct and promised victory; no independent cosmological mapping is being expounded here.
